person_note: The event quotations repeatedly expose Lucy as a participating retrospective I-narrator, including material from the hospital stay, childhood, family relationships, writing life, and later marriage. Dialogue and gnomic quotations were not allowed to vote mechanically; embedded speech and general reflections were marked non-base where appropriate. The authorized opening independently confirms sustained first-person narration, while several whole-book reviews identify Lucy as the narrator and describe the broader novel as her retrospective account. Targeted searches found no credible evidence of alternating, second-person, third-person, epistolary, or autonomous embedded narration. The opening source alone has limited scope, but its agreement with numerous interior quotations and multiple whole-book descriptions supports high confidence.
